calibrated_uncertainty_comparison.interpretation: The at_nominal_dft interval is the module's own claim for pure formulation-arithmetic precision (excludes operator DFT-control variance): the LAMBDA bias is ~29x that interval's half-width. Even against the wider as_applied_with_dft_control interval (which folds in an UNRELATED +/-20% operator DFT-control tolerance), the LAMBDA bias is still a majority-sized, wholly separate, systematic (unidirectional) effect that the module's error budget has no term for at all -- GUM (JCGM 100:2008 sec 3.2.3, 6.3.1) requires known systematic effects to be corrected before an expanded uncertainty is reported as a coverage interval for the measurand; this one is neither corrected nor disclosed.

overall_verdict_reasoning: coverage-spreading-v1's WFT/TC engine (KA4 closure: WFT*VS_frac==DFT exactly) assumes void-free close packing with zero PVC/CPVC awareness -- confirmed by direct inspection: none of its 9 known-answer-battery cases and no field in applied_spec/does_not_close reference PVC, CPVC, or porosity. The module's OWN sibling receipt reduced-pvc-porosity-v1 (signed two days later) already established that above CPVC a real dry film's volume is amplified by LAMBDA=PVC/CPVC, and named exactly this iron-oxide-red-primer-at-PVC-0.50 case as its worked in-domain example -- but that finding was never propagated back into coverage-spreading-v1 as a repair, supersession, or disclosed scope caveat. Applying coverage-spreading-v1's own signed WFT prescription (190.30 um, unchanged) to this in-domain porous primer at its own declared 127 um DFT target delivers an actual film build of 151.8 um, a 19.5% overshoot -- roughly 29x the receipt's own at_nominal_dft calibrated 95% interval half-width (0.67% relative) and a wholly unmodeled systematic effect even against the wider as-applied interval. The below-CPVC control case shows zero divergence (LAMBDA=1 exactly), confirming the bias is the CPVC/porosity effect specifically, not an artifact of this reimplementation. The claim 'COVERAGE_SPREADING_ENGINE_READY' as currently signed overclaims: it is READY only for the (undisclosed) below-CPVC subset of the module's own declared applicability domain.
